themes_detail.label: Bus Stop Shelter Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Bus stop shelter complaints have skyrocketed 3900% THIS WEEK (5 complaints vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), suggesting a sudden infrastructure failure or new construction disruption affecting transit access in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens.
evidence: 5 bus stop shelter complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 average (z-score: 14.74)
No prior sustained shelter complaint pattern in 90-day dataset
Affects daily commuters relying on public transit in two neighborhoods
reporting_angles: Investigate which bus stops are affected and why complaints spiked suddenly—damage, removal, or construction?
Interview MTA and community members about access and timing of repairs

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park-related noise complaints have jumped 967% THIS WEEK (4 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average), indicating a potential new event venue, construction, or recreational activity disrupting public green space in this district.
evidence: 4 noise complaints from parks THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 average (z-score: 5.21)
Community board has repeatedly requested 'enhance park safety through more security staff'
Coincides with summer season when park usage typically peaks
reporting_angles: Which parks are affected (Prospect Park, Carroll Park, etc.) and what's causing the noise?
Are permit-less events or gatherings occurring, or is there new construction near parks?

themes_detail.label: Tree Planting Demand Surge
themes_detail.summary: New tree requests have spiked 1100% THIS WEEK (3 requests vs. 0.2 weekly average), suggesting grassroots environmental engagement or response to recent tree loss—possibly linked to the 367 damaged tree complaints in the 90-day baseline.
evidence: 3 new tree requests THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 average (z-score: 6.35)
Baseline shows 367 damaged tree complaints over 90 days—residents may be seeking to replace losses
Aligns with community board's long-standing request to 'reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity'
reporting_angles: Are residents responding to visible tree damage from storm or disease?
Interview Parks Dept on capacity to meet planting demand and timeline

themes_detail.label: Traffic Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints rose 540% 2 WEEKS AGO (8 complaints vs. 1.2 weekly average), indicating a sustained transportation issue—possibly linked to construction, lane closures, or transit detours affecting commuter routes.
evidence: 8 traffic complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.56)
Timing suggests sustained issue beyond single incident
Overlaps with active ULURP projects (46 Nelson Street, Gowanus Canal work) that could cause routing disruption
reporting_angles: Map which streets are congested and connect to ongoing construction/ULURP milestones
Interview DOT about temporary lane closures or bus reroutes

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked 3100% 2 WEEKS AGO (4 complaints vs. 0.1 weekly average), suggesting either vendor proliferation, code violations, or sanitation issues that warrant investigation.
evidence: 4 mobile food vendor complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 average (z-score: 11.72)
No sustained follow-up complaints in past week suggests issue may have been addressed
Could indicate seasonal street vendor activity or permitting disputes
reporting_angles: What specific vendor violations triggered complaints—sanitation, obstruction, or unlicensed operation?
